title: Suji Appe with Coriander Chutney and Salad
steps: Combine suji (semolina) and curd in a mixing bowl to make a thick batter. Let it rest for 15–20 minutes.
Wash, peel, and chop the carrot into small cubes. Steam the carrot.
Boil a handful of peas until soft and tender.
Check the suji batter. Add a pinch of turmeric, jeera powder, black pepper powder, and enough water to achieve a pouring consistency.
Add the chopped vegetables to the batter.
Heat an appe pan and lightly grease it with ghee. Add mustard seeds and let them splutter.
Pour the batter into the molds and cook over low to medium heat until golden brown on both sides.
Serve warm with coriander chutney and salad.
notes: Suitable for babies aged 8 months and older, as indicated in the source.

title: Avocado Pancakes
steps: Mash the avocado and banana together.
Mix in the egg, flour, and cinnamon.
Cook on a greased pan until done.

title: Veggie Sticks
steps: Steam the apple, sweet potato, carrot, and lentils.
Mash everything together.
Mix in the oat flour and mozzarella.
Roll the mixture into balls.
Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.

title: Cheese Broccoli and Potato Bites
steps: Peel the potato, cut it into pieces, and steam for about 15 minutes until soft and mashable.
Dice the broccoli into small florets and steam for 7–10 minutes until soft.
Add the steamed potato and broccoli to a bowl and mash well.
Add the flour and shredded cheese. Mix until well combined.
Shape the mixture into sticks.
Bake at 350°F for 15 minutes.
Let cool before serving.

title: Masoor Dal and Oats Cheela
steps: Soak the masoor dal for 3 hours.
Blend the soaked masoor dal with the oats, carrot, ginger, turmeric, cumin powder, and coriander powder to make a smooth batter.
Adjust the batter consistency so it is neither too thick nor too thin.
Heat a pan and grease it with ghee.
Pour the batter onto the pan and cook on both sides.
notes: The source describes the cheelas as soft, healthy, and protein-rich.

title: Avocado Paratha
steps: Mash the avocado well.
Add the paneer, spinach, whole wheat flour, coriander powder, cumin powder, and ajwain.
Mix to make a soft dough without adding water.
Let the dough rest for 10 minutes.
Roll out the dough
Cook with a little ghee until soft and lightly golden.
notes: The natural moisture from the avocado helps form a soft dough without water and keeps the parathas tender. Skip salt for babies under 1 year. The source describes this recipe as suitable for babies aged 8 months and older and toddlers.

title: Healthy Kiwi Muffins
steps: Blend the kiwi and banana until smooth.
Add the oat flour, milk powder, and egg. Mix well.
Stir in the baking powder.
Pour the mixture into silicone molds.
Air fry at 180°C (350°F) for 10 minutes, or until cooked through.
notes: The source describes these muffins as a naturally sweet, soft snack suitable for babies aged 8 months and older.

title: Pumpkin Ragi Cake
ingredients: Optional: Pinch of cinnamon or cardamom
steps: Whisk the ragi flour, baking powder, and optional spices together in a bowl.
Stir in the pumpkin puree and curd until you have a smooth, thick batter.
Pour the batter into a lightly greased heat-proof bowl or ramekin.
Place the bowl in a steamer and steam on medium heat for 15–18 minutes, or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Let the cake cool, remove it from the bowl, and cut it into baby-safe strips or pieces.
notes: Suitable for babies aged 7 months and older. The cinnamon or cardamom is optional. The source recommends serving the cooled cake in baby-safe strips or pieces.

title: Moong Dal Paneer Chilla
notes: Easy to digest and packed with plant-based protein, iron, and fiber. Paneer added for an extra protein and calcium boost.

title: Sattu Laddoos
notes: Melt-in-the-mouth, soft, non-choking, and rolled to the perfect size for little hands practicing their pincer grasp. Safe for 7+ months. Milk is used to bind everything into a soft, smooth, age-appropriate texture.

title: Instant Veggie Dosa
ingredients: Handful of veggies (Carrot, beetroot, tomato, onion, cilantro)
steps: Soak sooji, poha, and makhana in water for 10 mins.
In a grinder, add soaked ingredients, veggies, and black pepper. Blend into a smooth batter.
Heat a pan with ghee. Pour small pancake-sized portions of batter.
Cook on low-medium heat for 2 mins per side until golden and cooked through.
notes: Suitable for 8+ month babies. No fermentation needed. Soft, fluffy, and easy for little hands to hold for BLW or picky eaters.
